discussion_comments.comment_body: Is a 2 minute `firstChunkMs` safe for hosted reasoning models? From what I can see in `streamText` (ai 7.0.120), the first chunk and chunk timers only reset on non-empty `text-delta`, `reasoning-delta` or `tool-input-delta` parts (plus `file`/`tool-call`). So a model that thinks for a while without streaming any reasoning text gets aborted as `before_first_chunk` even though the request is fine, and high effort runs can easily sit there past 2 minutes. Maybe only apply `firstChunkMs` when `timeoutMs` is set explicitly, or give it a much longer default than the header timeout?

discussion_comments.comment_body: i reverted back to the standard 5 minute timeout, this PR just improved error messaging and adds metrics now.

On LM Studio's `/api/v0/models`, `max_context_length` is the model's ceiling, and a loaded model also reports `loaded_context_length`, which is what it actually serves (can be a lot smaller). Since maxInputTokens falls back to contextWindow and that's the compaction budget, compaction won't kick in before LM Studio starts rejecting. Prefer `loaded_context_length` when it's present?

Fixed in 2c1a7f7d7: normalization now recurses into `items` (object and tuple forms) and into `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf` branches before the object-likeness gate, so nested uppercase types lowercase at every depth. Covered by the new "normalizes nested array items and combinator branches" test.

Fixed in 595b17fec: the object-likeness early return now applies only below the root. A bare or scalar-only root schema (empty MCP inputSchema included) still comes out as `{ type: "object" }`, matching what Gemini requires for tool parameters. Covered by the new root-default test.

That case exercised none of Cline's routing; it only pinned how `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` translates an id it classifies itself, which belongs to the adapter's own suite. The remaining cases pin what goes through Cline's resolver, catalog lookup and portable-reasoning path, and the live run in the PR body records Nova 2 Lite's accepted request shape.

Registering the model only takes model *selection* off the catalog; `resolveBedrockModelId` still consults it, and with #14480 on main the bare `openai.gpt-6-astra` case goes out as `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` in us-east-1.
